items.title: China's CXMT Stock Soars 470% in Start of Trading, Amid A.I. Race
items.content: China's leading memory chipmaker CXMT surged ~466-470% on its STAR Market debut, becoming the most valuable company on the Shanghai Stock Exchange. The IPO raised at least $8.6 billion, China's biggest since 2010.

items.title: CXMT 466% market debut makes it the most valuable China-listed company
items.content: Shares of Changxin Technology Group soared in its debut on Shanghai's STAR Market on Monday. By Tuesday, the ripple effect triggered a global tech rout as China's AI chip breakthrough rattled markets.

items.title: China's AI chip breakthrough triggers global tech rout
items.content: Global tech stocks plunged on Tuesday after China achieved a breakthrough in developing technology crucial to the AI boom, sparking a worldwide sell-off in semiconductor and AI-related shares.

items.title: Stock market today: Dow closes at record, S&P 500 flat
items.content: The Dow gained 0.51% (262 points) to close at 52,210.08 — a record high. The S&P added just 0.02% to 7,413.18. Tech stocks continued to suffer as investors rotated out of AI stocks amid spending concerns.

items.title: Stock market today: Live updates July 28
items.content: Hong Kong's Hang Seng up 0.31% in late trading Tuesday. Mainland China's CSI 300 closed 2.83% lower at 4,569.52, dragged by tech losses. Hang Seng futures pointed to a higher open at 25,020.

items.title: Stocks Rise Early as U.S. and Iran Pause Attacks
items.content: U.S. stocks opened higher as the U.S. and Iran paused attacks, easing Middle East tensions. Oil prices dropped sharply, providing relief after weeks of Strait of Hormuz disruptions.

items.title: Hang Seng Index edges higher as U.S.–Iran pause eases oil prices
items.content: Hong Kong shares opened slightly firmer Monday after signs of easing tensions in the Middle East helped steady investor sentiment and sent oil prices sharply lower.

items.title: US military says it fired on merchant vessel breaching blockade of Iranian ports
items.content: The U.S. military fired on a merchant vessel attempting to breach its blockade of Iranian ports, while Iran targeted American strongholds around the Persian Gulf. Strait of Hormuz remains a flashpoint.

items.title: Iran Digs In After Latest Trump Threat on Civilian Targets
items.content: Iran's IRGC said an oil tanker caught fire after an explosion while trying to pass a mined route south of the Strait of Hormuz. Two other tankers turned back. Tensions remain extremely high despite June MoU.

items.title: 2026 Iran war: June MoU seeks to reopen Strait of Hormuz
items.content: Despite the June 2026 MoU seeking to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and end the Iran war, Iran continues to assert hegemonic control and seeks to collect fees on ships passing through.

items.title: 4 Big Tech earnings reports, a Fed meeting, and $100 oil: Busiest week of the quarter
items.content: Alphabet beat revenue and profit expectations. Intel reported Q2 2026 earnings of $0.42/share, beating estimates of $0.21, but stock fell 7.9%. Big Tech earnings continue this week alongside Fed meeting.

items.title: Weekly market commentary: Middle East escalation risk
items.content: BlackRock notes markets have reacted less sharply to Middle East escalation, even as the global economy has fewer buffers against a prolonged energy shock. Geopolitical risk remains elevated.

items.title: Stock Market News: Tech stocks suffer as AI rotation continues
items.content: Tech stocks continued to suffer as investors rotated out of AI-related stocks on concerns over massive investments. Intel fell 7.9% despite beating earnings and raising profit forecast.

items.title: Global Markets Weekly Update: Business activity slows
items.content: Preliminary business surveys showed activity expanding at its slowest pace in more than four years, led by weaker services and manufacturing growth as geopolitical uncertainty weighed on sentiment.

items.title: Why Geopolitics Has Overtaken Supply And Demand In Commodity Markets
items.content: Geopolitical tensions have disrupted supply chains and increased processing costs across critical minerals sector. Even obscure inputs like sulphuric acid are now concerns.
